title: Sale Banner Maker for Square Offer Images | AIVideosUGC
description: Move stock with a sale image that leaves clean space for your offer. One product photo becomes a square banner; add the discount and dates yourself.
h1: Sale Banner Maker with Room for the Offer
lead: A candle shop can lead the feed with this weekend's price. Set the jar in a sale square and put Saturday's end date where the eye lands first.
steps_h2: How to Make a Sale Banner in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: Open a layout, set the product and the offer, then post the square.

steps.d: Upload one clear photo of the product on offer. The template supplies a square composition made for a feed.
Place the discount, code, and event dates so the promotion leads. The price reaches scrollers first.
Download the square and publish it on Instagram. The offer is large enough to read in the feed.

faq.q: What is an Instagram sale post template?
faq.a: A square that keeps the product recognizable while the promotion is easy to read. A mug can fill the frame, with the member price large enough to read on a phone.

faq.q: How do I make a sale post?
faq.a: Upload a product photo, choose a sale scene, place the offer you approved, and download the square. Check it on a phone, then post.

faq.q: Can the post show my discount and the event date?
faq.a: Yes. The layout is there so the promotion leads. You enter the percent, the code, and the dates that match the sale you approved, then read them back before publishing.

faq.q: What size is the sale image?
faq.a: Square, which fits an Instagram or Facebook feed post. For a wide site header, place that square on a wider background in your design tool.

faq.q: Can I reuse one scene for a later promotion?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the product scene and change the headline. One week can be a percent off, and the next can be a different approved line.

faq.q: Can I make a tall Story from the sale square?
faq.a: The template gives you a square. For a tall Story or Reel, set that square on a 9:16 background after download.

faq.q: Where should the discount code go?
faq.a: In the open part of the layout, as text you can still edit. Read the full offer on a phone-sized preview before the ad runs.

faq.q: How many credits does a sale photo use?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. The cost is shown before you start, and a failed job returns those credits. The download has no watermark. You can use it in your ads, pages, and posts. You are responsible for the offer terms.

faq.q: What should I do when the sale ends?
faq.a: Pause or replace the post so an old date or code is not still up. The product scene can stay for a later promotion or as a plain listing image.

faq.q: Can I start from a holiday scene and change it later?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the product scene and swap the headline when the holiday passes. Seasonal notes live on [Black Friday ad creatives](page:occ-black-friday).

faq.q: Do I need a paid subscription for a sale post?
faq.a: Yes. Photos, batches, and API jobs all draw from one paid-plan balance.

reviews.h2: Sale Scenes Sellers Build from One Photo
reviews.lead: A few ways sellers use one product photo as the scene behind an offer.

items.d: The shop generates a seasonal scene and types the percent, code and end date in its editor. When the number changes, the text you added changes and the product scene can stay.

items.t: End date kept out of the file
items.d: The end date is not generated into the image, so an expired promotion is removed by deleting the text you added. The product photo underneath can be reused.
The same scene carries a percent-off line in one ad and a different approved line in another. Both lines are added after download.
An empty area is left for the code, then checked on a phone-sized preview before the ad is published. The code is typed later, not asked for in the picture.
The square image goes in a Facebook or Instagram feed, or on the product page, after the final offer is added. A wide site header means placing it on a wider background in the editor.

items.t: No new shoot for the event
items.d: They start from a product photo they already have instead of booking a banner shoot. Claims and offer terms stay their responsibility.

definition.title: What Is an Instagram Sale Post?
paras: It is the square a shop uses when a tote bag's price changes for a long weekend. The bag stays fully visible, and the last day sits where a thumb stops.
You are filling in a feed square, not drawing one. Next month, the same tote can carry a new headline for a different event.

reasons.h2: Why Sellers Start From a Sale Template
reasons.lead: The square should make the promotion obvious to someone scrolling the shop's feed.

items.d: A thumb on the feed should meet the mug's Saturday price before it meets the handle. The mug stays in the frame so the shopper still knows what is on offer.
The feed frame is already composed. You set the scarf in it, and the price is already sitting where the eye lands.
Use the scarf square on the feed and again on the product page. When the next event starts, only the headline changes, so the shop still looks like the same shop.

more_sections.h2: Picture Tools for a Sale Post
more_sections.lead: Scene tools around the square, so the promotion still leads once the product is in place.

items.d: Place the product on white, on a see-through ground, in a new setting, or against a softer background. The product shape stays the one you uploaded.
An AI avatar can wear the item. You can also ask for a top-down photo, a garment with no visible mannequin, a softer shadow, or a cleaned product shot.
Resize the square, change a garment color, or remove a stray object. The offer stays as text, so the next headline is a quick edit.
Turn the same photo into a short clip when the feed needs motion, with a voiceover and captions if you want them. A video spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.
Run the same sale scene across many products, so a weekend catalog can go out in one pass.
Send product photos from your shop software through the API and bring the scenes back to your catalog.
